title: WPMS/2700/2022 of M/S KHURANA BROTHERS  A PARTNERSHIP FIRM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No.2700 of 2022
Shri Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Shri Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, learned counsel
for the petitioners.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned DAG for
the State.
The petitioners have preferred the
present writ petition to assail the Clause
17 of the Notice for selling of resin by
Public Auction (amended) contained in
letter No.1100/10-5 dated 29.10.2022,
Muni-Ki-Reti. The said Clause reads as
follows:-
"The rate of fee on the stamp fee is 02%
on the movable property for recovering the
value of resin by public auction under
Article 23 (B) of Schedule 1 (B) Indian
Stamp Act 1899 in the light of the letter
no.2221/10-2 (Stamp Fee) dated 8.3.2013
of Chief Conservator of Forest, Kumaon,
Uttarakhand, Nainital. If there are changes
in the rate of stamp fee by the Uttarakhand
Government then it will be binding on both
the parties. The proposal with regard to the
stamp fee has been sent to the
Government by Chief Wildlife Conservator
(HoFF) Uttarakhand vide its letter no.B-1165/10-2 dated 18.3.2021 letter no.B-627/10-2 dated 29.12.2021 and in the
aforesaid case whatever decision of the
State it will be valid to all. The resin
purchasers have to give affidavit with
regard to stamp fee in compliance of the
letter no.9664/10-5 (Stamp Fee) dated
15.10.2022 issued by the Chief
Conservator of Forest, Kumaon,
Uttarakhand, Nainital."
The submission of learned counsel for
the petitioners is that the respondents
should first get the process of revision of

2
stamp duty completed as per the proposal
dated 18.03.2021 and 29.12.2021 and
only thereafter, the tenders should be
invited. He submits that the petitioners
cannot be asked to pay the revised stamp
duty, if the same is revised during the
course of the contract.
The respondents have clearly
disclosed to the interested bidders that
the current stamp fee is 2 % and the
movable property for recovering the value
of resin by public auction under Article 23
(B) of Scheduled 1 (B) of the Indian
Stamp Act, 1899.
There is absolutely nothing
unreasonable in prescribing that if the
stamp fee rate is revised by the
Government of Uttarakhand, the same
would be binding on the parties. The
petitioners cannot insist that no tender
can be invited before the revision of
stamp duty takes place. In case, the
petitioners are not agreeable to the said
condition, it is open to the petitioners not
to participate in the tender in process.
We find absolutely no merit in the
present petition. Accordingly, the writ
petition is dismissed.
(R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)
 04.11.2022
AK/BS
